messages.author: 8043bac28d61c32f
messages.subject: Genetic map in Maize with a high density of SNPs and RILs
parts:
Hi Karl,

I am trying to make a genetic map in Maize with 164 RILs and a high density of SNPs.

I started out with 56.000 markers. I eliminated almost 40.000 markers due to missing data, monomorphic markers for both parents, and those markers with wrong segregation. 

I finally got 12.455 SNPs (distributed in the 10 maize chromosomes). I have got the chromosomes location for each marker, and also the physic distance of each marker.

I would like to calculate the genetic distance of each marker, so as to later do a QTL analysis.

I have been able to correctly use the function read.cross() and jittermap() functions. But I am having a bit of trouble using the est.rf, and others functions. My computer is not too good and I am working with a lot of markers (12.455 SNPs for the genetic map).  

This is the error I’ve got when running est.rf() function: Error: cannot allocate vector of size 926.7 Mb.

I was just wondering if I can continue my analysis working with each chromosome separately. 

Or maybe there is a way of reducing those 12.455 markers to a fewer number, so I can continue working with less markers. I dont know if there is a function to do this or if it is reazonable to do it.

What do you recommend me?

Thanks a lot,
Lucas A.

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Genetic map in Maize with a high density of SNPs and RILs
parts:
With 12,000 markers, you won't be able to run est.rf, because it will attempt to estimate (and store) the recombination fractions between all pairs of markers. You're running out of memory for this. I would focus just on est.map, to get estimates of inter-marker distances.

One trick that might be useful: use fill.geno to fill in all missing genotypes; estimate the map with this simplified data set. Then use that estimated map as a starting point when you go back to the original data that includes missing genotypes.

karl

However, I am still having some issues with my genetic map. I have not able to reduce the length of all chromosomes.

I should expect a correlation in the physical position and the genetic distance of each marker along the chromosome.


Thanks for everything,


Lucas A.

So, I constructed my map using the order I asigned based on their physical position instead of using ripple function.

Is this correct? 

Thanks for everything
Lucas A.

Dear Dr. Karl,

I read all the posts on this group related to genetic mapping in the presence of physical map.

Please help me in resolving my doubt.

I have a genetic map for which I also have the physical positions of markers.

How can I make best use of these physical positions of markers in improving the genetic map ?

I replaced the positions of genetic map with physical positions of markers and converted them in Mbp. Then I used the code following the example for "fake.f2" using the following code:

newmap <- est.map(chrom1phys)
logliks <- sapply(newmap, attr, "loglik")
chrom1physmap <- replace.map(chrom1phys, newmap)

I could not find the details of attr "loglik" in the help for est.map ? 

Is the methodology correct?

Thanks in advance.

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Re: Genetic map in Maize with a high density of SNPs and RILs
parts:
est.map() re-estimates the inter-marker genetic distances, taking the order of markers as fixed and known. 

The loglik attribute is the log likelihood for the order, which you can ignore because you are not comparing orders. 

karl
